doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Montreux Festival and 'Alone at Montreux'
summary: His first European trip was a solo set at Montreux, recorded by Atlantic.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Can you look at your career and pick out some really fond memories right now? Recording sessions or just particular nights where the group of musicians you were playing with was very just really outstanding? Is that possible with all the playing you’ve done over the years? Can you think back and say boy, I’m so glad that one happened?

Well I’ve had some outstanding nights, memorable nights, as a soloist and in some trio settings too. As a soloist my most memorable nights would be my first time in Europe ever. And I was called to play the Montreux Jazz Festival in Switzerland, that was my first time ever in Europe and I was doing a solo. I think that, I’m trying to remember who was on that night, I think they had maybe three or four different artists on that night, I think Stan Getz, Stan Getz’s group was playing, and I think Chuck Mangione’s group was playing, and me, solo. I mean I knew these guys you know, so when they saw me they said who’s with you? I said nobody. Are you kidding? I said I’m going to play solo. Okay. And I started to play. After they had played then it was my turn. And I was a little nervous or apprehensive or whatever, but after maybe a half a tune I realized that the audience was definitely with me. And it turned out to be one of the most enjoyable nights of my career.
You could just feel that kind of electricity?

Oh yes. And as luck would have it, Atlantic Records was recording that night and I was an Atlantic artist at the time, and they were recording “Alone at Montreux” came from that. Then on the basis of this record people around the world just liked this record, with the audience and everything, the audience participation, the applause and so forth. It turned out to be a great record for me, and as a result of that I was able to go on and play many places in the world that I might not have been able to.
